title: Smart routing: fix silent model-variant fallback during regional capacity overflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity spike on 2025-02-10 we observed a class of failures where the smart-routing layer quietly selected a fallback model variant that was functionally compatible but materially different in latency/cost/quality, and crucially did not annotate responses with the effective variant. Customers saw unexplained regressions in output tokenization and latency without obvious error codes.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-10 13:07 UTC: Spike in requests in eu-west-1 due to customer batch job.
- 2025-02-10 13:08–13:12 UTC: Router hit regional capacity threshold and triggered fallback policy.
- 2025-02-10 13:12–13:25 UTC: Some requests routed to alternate region and to lower-capacity model variant (v1-8q vs v1-16q).
- 2025-02-10 13:15 UTC: Observability alerts for increased P50/P95 latency and tokenization mismatches from eval probes.
- 2025-02-10 13:30 UTC: Ops rollback of an experimental routing policy; customer reports received.

Root cause analysis:
1) Policy bug in the compatibility matrix: model-variant compatibility comparator allowed variants with mismatched tokenizer configs to be considered 'compatible' when a minimum metadata flag was present. This allowed silent selection of a variant with different tokenization semantics.
2) Router omitted effective-variant metadata in the response header/body when a fallback was applied via cross-region reroute, so downstream clients couldn't programmatically detect fallback.
3) No synthetic test covered tokenization-preserving fallbacks across region or during autoscale events; regression wasn't caught in CI/chaos tests.
4) Dashboarding focused on error counts and token latency but not on 'variant drift' (fraction of responses where effective_variant != requested_variant).

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Reverted the experimental routing policy at 13:30 UTC (ENG-9123).
- Emergency config patch to the compatibility comparator to require tokenizer-id equality for fallbacks (hotfix deployed 13:50 UTC).
- Notified affected customers and opened support cases.

Action items (concrete, owners, deadlines):
1) Add explicit effective-variant metadata to all responses generated by the router and serve runtime (header + structured field). Owner: Luca Moretti. Due: 2025-02-25. Blocker: none. Ticket: ENG-9201.
2) Tighten compatibility comparator to only allow fallback if tokenizer-id and vocab-hash match OR if an explicit tokenizer-mapping is registered. Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2025-02-28. Ticket: ENG-9202.
3) Create a routing-chaos suite that simulates regional capacity evictions and asserts that: 1) fallbacks preserve tokenizer semantics, 2) effective-variant is annotated, 3) no silent quality regressions. Owner: SRE team (lead: Marco Ruiz). Due: 2025-03-12. Ticket: ENG-9203.
4) Dashboard metric: 'variant_drift_ratio' (per-model, per-region) and alert at >0.1% over 5m. Owner: Observability (Claire Nguyen). Due: 2025-02-27. Ticket: ENG-9210.
5) Backfill: run eval prompt set against recent traces during the incident window to quantify quality regression (report to PM). Owner: Applied ML (Eden Park). Due: 2025-02-24.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- All routed responses include effective-variant metadata in both APIs and SDK wrappers (JS/Python).
- Compatibility comparator unit tests + integration tests cover tokenizer-id and vocab-hash mismatch cases.
- Routing-chaos suite added to CI gating for routing service.

Related artifacts and links:
- Incident notes (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/INC-271-fallback-regression
- Hotfix PR (router): https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1882
- Compatibility comparator change (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/modelsync/pull/431
- Dashboard snapshot (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dash/123456/routing-variant-drift (internal)

Risks and trade-offs considered:
- Requiring tokenizer-id equality may reduce fallback flexibility during rare legitimate compatibility mappings; mitigated by supporting an explicit tokenizer-mapping registry (owners to maintain).
- Adding metadata increases response size slightly; judged acceptable because metadata can be encoded in a compact header and optionally disabled for low-bandwidth clients.

Notes on customer communication:
- PMs to coordinate a short postmortem email to affected customers summarizing root cause, mitigations, and ETA for follow-ups. Link: PM-402.

Next steps (short term):
- Kick off ENG-9201 and ENG-9202 immediately; pair-programming session scheduled 2025-02-21 (Luca + Priya).
- Observability to ship variant_drift metric by 2025-02-27.

Owners and reviewers:
- Incident lead: Aisha Patel
- Routing lead: Luca Moretti
- Applied ML reviewer: Eden Park
- SRE reviewer: Marco Ruiz
